lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: understanding a pay statement and schedule

objective: Learners correctly identify each line of a sample pay statement and verify that gross pay minus deductions equals net pay, so they can read a real one with confidence later without this lesson claiming to predict what any real statement will show.
scenario: Given an annotated, entirely fictional sample pay statement with invented figures for gross pay, a few generic deduction line items, and net pay, the learner labels each part, checks the arithmetic, and writes two questions they would ask a real employer's payroll or HR contact if a real statement's line looked wrong.
safetyNotes: This is not tax, payroll, or financial advice — real pay statements vary by employer, location, and situation, and this lesson only teaches how to read the parts of a sample.
No real pay statement, real employer, or real income figure is required or should be entered anywhere.
materials: the provided fictional sample pay statement

tasks.directions: Before labeling, guess what you think 'gross pay' and 'net pay' mean.

prompts.text: In your own words, before checking, what do you think 'gross pay' and 'net pay' mean, and which one do you think is usually the bigger number?

tasks.directions: Label each line of the fictional sample pay statement.

prompts.text: I correctly labeled the gross pay line.
I correctly labeled each of the generic deduction line items.
I correctly labeled the net pay line.

tasks.directions: Verify the arithmetic and write two questions for a real payroll or HR contact.

prompts.text: Show that gross pay minus the listed deductions equals the stated net pay. Then write two specific questions you'd ask a real employer's payroll or HR contact if a real line item ever looked wrong to you.
Was your warm-up guess about gross versus net pay correct? What surprised you most about the sample statement?

remediation: If the learner's arithmetic check doesn't actually reconcile (gross minus deductions doesn't equal the stated net), reteach by having them add the deductions one at a time against a running total until the discrepancy is visible and correctable.
extension: Have the learner design one additional fictional deduction line item not on the sample, add it to the statement, and recompute net pay correctly.
